Absence Reporting
In the event of your child being absent, parents are asked to let the school know before 9am on every day of absence. A message can be left on our dedicated absence line when you telephone (choose Option 1 and wait for both beeps before recording your message). The school will contact families when no message is received. This ensures that the school has no cases of unauthorised absence and that children cannot play truant.
Please ensure that your child is fully recovered before sending them back to school as they will be unable to work well if they feel ill.
Please let us know if your child picks up impetigo, head lice etc. In this way, all parents can be warned to be on the lookout and stop the spread of infection. If your child becomes unwell while at school, you will be contacted so as you can take your child home. It is most important that your contact information is therefore kept up to date so please let the office know of any changes. In the event of an accident or illness which requires emergency treatment, a senior staff member will take the child to hospital while the school office contacts you. A member of staff will stay with your child until you arrive at hospital.
If your child has medicine which needs to be taken at regular intervals, parents must complete a form from the school office. All medicine is kept in our office area, not classrooms. Only the office staff or Headteacher can administer medicine. The Headteacher has the right to ask parents to administer the medicine if necessary.

Friends of Queensway
The FoQ is an organisation of parents, grandparents and carers who, alongside school teachers and staff, encourage closer links between school and home. The FoQ are best known for their fundraising work with a useful social function too.
We have two purposes of equal importance. Firstly, we raise money to help fund activities and equipment that the school can’t fund from its normal budget. Secondly, we also provide social opportunities and fun activities for everyone to enjoy together, helping to promote the family and community atmosphere that is so important to our children’s experience of school. The FoQ committee and Mrs Horbury-Jakeman, Headteacher, will decide together on how the funds raised will be spent. Once your child joins the school, you automatically become a FoQ member, so come and join one of our meetings to have your say! We would love to see you there.
We are always looking for people to help us to carry out our events. As the saying goes, many hands make light work – this is so true! We also understand that many parents work, have younger children at home and the general day-to-day pressures of life can all mean that free time is in short supply. However, if you can and would like to help, we would love for you to get involved.
How to get involved: When we have an event, we will send an email or letter home. If you can support that event in any way, then please respond by return of email or calling in to the school office. We will then contact you to discuss things further.

Nursery
Our school was very excited to open our new Nursery in September 2019, and it has quickly grown from strength to strength. The class is open to children aged 3 and 4 years of age. Queensway Nursery does not offer provision for 2-year-old children.
The aim is to build upon the continuing success of our Reception Stage and give children a positive start to school life in a secure and nurturing environment.
Our Nursery has its own spacious classroom and outside play area adjacent to the 2 Reception Classes. The staff team includes a Nursery Leader and two Teaching Assistants who are highly experienced Early Years practitioners.
Entitlement starts from the term following your child's 3rd birthday:
Admissions are three times a year, for as long as places are available. Funding and entitlement are based on a three-term year, with children starting in September, January and April.
The school has set a termly deadline for considering applications for admission into the following term as set out below. As we have a maximum of 26 full-time places (30 hours per week) or 52 part-time places (15 hours per week) available each academic year, we strongly recommend returning your application as soon as possible rather than waiting until the deadline.
If we receive more applications than there are places available, we will allocate places fairly using the criteria set out in our Nursery Policy. All nursery places are term-time only.
The 15-hour provision is for 5 mornings (8:30am-11:30am) or 5 afternoons (12:00pm-15:00pm), 5 days a week, term time only (38 weeks per year). Other patterns of attendance cannot be accommodated (cannot be a mixture of mornings and afternoons). However, requests for a child who attends for 15 hours to access extra sessions on a paid basis will be considered if there is capacity and this would be at a cost of £14.00 for one morning or afternoon session. School meals can also be purchased via Fresh Start at an additional cost of £2.70 per day for children accessing the 30-hour provision, unless your child is eligible for free school meals.
From September 2017, families meeting certain eligibility criteria are now legally entitled to a funded early years place of 30 hours per week. Information on this entitlement is available at https://www.gov.uk/30-hours-free-childcare. This provision will be from 9:00am-15:00pm, 5 days a week, term time only (38 weeks per year). Parents can apply for their funding codes via HMRC. It is recommended to parents that they do not apply earlier than 3 months before the term in which they become eligible to avoid having to reconfirm their code prior to starting in the relevant term.
Children eligible for this extended entitlement may access 15 hours at Queensway (5 mornings or 5 afternoons) and use the remaining 15 hours with another provider, such as a childminder etc.
As our Nursery will be part of Queensway's educational setting, the uniform for nursery children will be the same as for our school-aged children. Please see uniform information provided under the Parent Information tab. The link for our page on Cross Embroidery's website is https://www.crossembroidery.com/schoolwear/46-queensway-school

Extra Curriculum Clubs
Through our programme of extra-curricular clubs, both within and beyond the school day, we aim to provide experiences that enrich and support our curriculum. Mainly, clubs are led by school staff, although occasionally we may offer clubs that are led by specialist providers, for example Cherwell Theatre Company. At any time, a wide range of clubs is on offer – our programme of clubs and activities available is revised termly depending on the time of year and other commitments children may have. Clubs on offer at Queensway vary through the year, but have included African Drumming, Lego, Rounders, Choir, Origami, Wildlife Rangers, Art Club and Library Club.

Parents are very welcome to visit us when choosing their child's school.
As soon as you think you might like your child to attend our school, please contact us to register your interest.

Reception Class
All children are eligible for a full-time place at school in the September following their 4th birthday. Places are allocated at our school in accordance with the Oxfordshire Local Authority Admission Policy and full details can be found on the Oxfordshire County Council website at https://www.oxfordshire.gov.uk/schools. If you are applying for a Reception place in school, you will need to complete a Primary Application Form and return it to either the school or County Hall. The telephone number for the Oxfordshire Admissions Team is 01865 815175.
If you wish to come to Queensway School and live in our catchment area, you have priority and will be offered a place if there is a space.
If you live outside the catchment area you will be offered a place if one is available. The Local Authority considers all applications and will contact you if your child cannot attend the school of your choice. Further guidance about the LA Admissions Policy is available in the booklet 'Oxfordshire Schools Admissions and Transfers', which is published annually by the LA.
Queensway's Published Admission Number (PAN) which is the maximum number of children that can be admitted into our Reception Year, is 60.
Applications for Reception can be made from November 2026 until January 2027. If your child already attends our Nursery, they WILL NOT automatically transfer to Reception. The application process applies to all current Nursery children who are due to start school in September 2027 (birthdates between 1 September 2022 and 31 August 2023).

School Trips
The Governors of the school have to determine their own policy for charging for school activities beyond the normal school budget. The Governors of this school have decided to adopt a policy of voluntary contributions to meet the cost of any planned visits, residential courses and other activities such as visiting speakers. These are beyond the normal school budget and, although parents can now decline to contribute, no child will be excluded from participating. If insufficient voluntary contributions are received, events may need to be cancelled. Parents experiencing difficulties in these matters should contact the Headteacher in the strictest confidence.
We work to a £20 per child limit for the total cost of trips in one academic year that we will ask parents for.

Wrap Around Care
Breakfast Club – Reception to Year 6
Breakfast Club runs daily in the school hall and is available at a cost of £2.50 per child, per day, from 7:45am with last admission into Breakfast Club at 8:15am. Booking and payment in advance is to be made via ParentPay. Please click here to log on to ParentPay to make a booking. Children can choose from a range of cereals, toast, juices, water and milk.
We would remind parents that Breakfast Club starts at 7:45am and children should NOT be on site, unsupervised, before then. Thank you.
After School Club – Reception to Year 6
Together with our Breakfast Club, we are also able to provide a full term-time childcare service on-site for children from when they start in Reception Class to Year 6 at Queensway School. Reception pupils are admitted following individual assessment to ensure suitability.
The club will run from 3pm until 6pm daily at a cost of £3.75 per hour and children will have the opportunity to take part in all sorts of fun activities, and those staying after 4.30pm will receive a hot, light snack. Further details are available in the attached Contract and Information Booklet for Parents/Carers.
Parents will need to book. For further details and a booking form, please contact the school office on 01295 251631 or email to childcare@queensway.oxon.sch.uk

Platinum School Games Mark
We are delighted to announce that Queensway has been awarded the Platinum School Games Mark, celebrating commitment to school sport and physical activity.
The School Games Mark recognises schools that go above and beyond in providing opportunities for all pupils to take part in high-quality PE, competitive sport, and extra-curricular activities.
Achieving the Platinum award is an outstanding achievement, reflecting dedication, teamwork, and a whole-school approach to promoting active, healthy lifestyles.
